inconsistencies: #34038 and #35387 are competing solutions to the same problem (trace logging unusable without paired -debug, no runtime control). Only one should be merged; review #34038 first since #35355 is built on top of it.

#36778 (delete the loadtxoutset RPC in favour of a startup arg) and #33117 (expose loadtxoutset through interfaces::Node so the GUI can call it at runtime) pull in opposite directions. The #36778 decision gates whether #33117 is worth reviewing at all.
#36200 and #36204 both harden the same HTTP server against worker/connection exhaustion and touch adjacent code; review them as a pair, #36200 first (trivially triggerable).
#36753 and #36758 both rewrite HTTP status-code and JSON-RPC error semantics in httprpc; they will conflict. #36758 fixes an assertion crash, so it should go first.
#36855 and #36864 are the same watch-only deprecation cleanup split across RPCs; #35433 is the same deprecation discipline for `replaceable`. Batch them.
#36566 changes private-broadcast return semantics that #36477's reporting builds on; review #36566 first.
#36626 and #36851 are both test-only additions to rpc_psbt.py; #36626 (demonstrated mutation-survival gap) is the one worth a reviewer's time first.
#36005 and #35370 both concern key-origin/derivation metadata exposed through descriptor and PSBT RPCs; reviewing them together would keep the warning and strip semantics coherent.
#35054 presupposes the assumeutxo direction that #36778 is trying to change; its downloadutxoset RPC should not be reviewed ahead of that decision.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: one credential-leak P1, a block of HTTP/REST/JSON-RPC correctness-and-security fixes plus a few substantial interface features at P2, a long P3 tail of single-RPC bug fixes and additive fields, and a small P4 group of cleanups and tests. Two bands were adjusted for cross-PR consistency: #36002 raised to P2 to sit with #34534 (both remove a long-standing pruned-node workaround for external callers), and #31672 lowered to P4 because the category explicitly ranks new fields without an external consumer low, matching its own 'marginal' rationale.
